correctness.rationale: The conditional law follows from stationarity of every smooth function of \(z\): \(\mathbb E[x^2\mid z]=bz\). Differentiating the displayed polynomial coboundary gives \(W'=y^2-bz(z-1)\); completing the square yields the stated height defect. The zero-defect case forces \(y=0\), \(x^2=bz\), and then invariance forces the three equilibria. For a non-equilibrium stationary measure, the prior balance gives positive mass on \(z>1\); restricting the conditional law to that set forces positive mass where simultaneously \(z>1\) and \(x^2>b\). Thus the assigned statements are mathematically correct.
